title: Using technology to keep employees happy
paragraphs: Going to work can be a slog, especially if your job is full of tedious tasks and pointless meetings. Obviously, work is necessary to earn an income, and if you get good job satisfaction it’s a bonus! But what can make it more worthwhile are the extra perks that your employer offers you as a reward for your loyalty and commitment.

Employee benefits are commonplace these days. Traditionally, these have included a good pension and extra days off work. But when a job used to be for life, there wasn’t much incentive to try and keep staff. Now millennials look to leave their jobs within the first two years, and when they are seeking a position, they want to know the benefits they’ll get on top of their pay. These include half-price cinema tickets, cycle to work schemes and gym passes.

But these perks come at a cost to an employer, and now technology is being used to discover if and when they offer value for money. Writing for the BBC, Jessica Bown says “Emerging technologies such as data analytics, chatbots, and wearables can help employers know which benefits resonate with employees.” The idea is to avoid wasting money on things that don’t get used and enable a company to tailor what it can offer to attract and retain the right staff.

As an example, at merchant bank, Close Brothers, AI has been used to develop chatbots that can help employees to find information on subjects ranging from mental health to saving for retirement at any time. And Microsoft has developed software to help businesses track their employee’s wellbeing needs. Anna Rasmussen, founder of Open Blend, told the BBC “It shows companies what their employees need to stay motivated and reach their full potential in real-time.” Insurance company Vitality offer wearable technology to track employees’ movements. Staff can earn ‘rewards’ by having their activity tracked. A study found that by measuring participant’s performance, they did the equivalent of 4.8 extra days of activity per month.

It seems that if used in the right way, technology can provide greater engagement between an employee and the company. That can lead to a happier, healthier and committed work force. But human resources experts warn against relying solely on tech for deciding on employee benefits provision. Greater understanding of new technology and how it’s used is needed, they say.

vocabulary.entry: slog /slɒɡ/ n. 苦差事；艰辛的工作
vocabulary.example: The project was a real slog, but we finished it on time.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目真是件苦差事，但我们还是按时完成了。

vocabulary.entry: tedious /ˈtiːdiəs/ adj. 单调乏味的；冗长的
vocabulary.example: I find data entry very tedious.
vocabulary.translation: 我觉得数据录入非常单调乏味。

vocabulary.entry: pointless /ˈpɔɪntləs/ adj. 无意义的；徒劳的
vocabulary.example: It's pointless arguing with him—he never listens.
vocabulary.translation: 和他争论毫无意义，他从来不听。

vocabulary.entry: job satisfaction /dʒɒb ˌsætɪsˈfækʃn/ 工作满足感
vocabulary.example: She gets a lot of job satisfaction from helping people.
vocabulary.translation: 她从帮助别人中获得了很大的工作满足感。

vocabulary.entry: perk /pɜːk/ n. 额外福利；津贴
vocabulary.example: One of the perks of the job is free travel.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作的额外福利之一是免费旅行。

vocabulary.entry: loyalty /ˈlɔɪəlti/ n. 忠诚；忠心
vocabulary.example: Her loyalty to the company was never in doubt.
vocabulary.translation: 她对公司的忠诚从未受到质疑。

vocabulary.entry: commitment /kəˈmɪtmənt/ n. 奉献；投入
vocabulary.example: The job requires a high level of commitment.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作需要高度的投入。

vocabulary.entry: employee benefit /ɪmˈplɔɪiː ˈbenɪfɪt/ 员工福利
vocabulary.example: The company offers excellent employee benefits, including health insurance.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司提供完善的员工福利，包括健康保险。

vocabulary.entry: pension /ˈpenʃn/ n. 养老金；退休金
vocabulary.example: He plans to retire early and live on his pension.
vocabulary.translation: 他计划提前退休，靠养老金生活。

vocabulary.entry: incentive /ɪnˈsentɪv/ n. 激励；诱因
vocabulary.example: The company offers a financial incentive for employees who meet targets.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司为达到目标的员工提供经济激励。

vocabulary.entry: millennial /mɪˈleniəl/ n. 千禧一代（通常指1980-2000年出生的人）
vocabulary.example: Millennials value work-life balance more than previous generations.
vocabulary.translation: 千禧一代比前几代人更看重工作与生活的平衡。

vocabulary.entry: cycle to work scheme /ˈsaɪkl tu wɜːk skiːm/ 骑行上班计划
vocabulary.example: I joined the cycle to work scheme and saved money on transport.
vocabulary.translation: 我加入了骑行上班计划，在交通上省了钱。

vocabulary.entry: gym pass /dʒɪm pɑːs/ 健身卡；健身房通行证
vocabulary.example: The company gives all staff a free gym pass.
vocabulary.translation: 公司为所有员工提供免费健身卡。

vocabulary.entry: value for money /ˈvæljuː fɔː ˈmʌni/ 物有所值
vocabulary.example: This laptop offers good value for money.
vocabulary.translation: 这台笔记本电脑物有所值。

vocabulary.entry: data analytics /ˈdeɪtə ˌænəˈlɪtɪks/ 数据分析
vocabulary.example: Data analytics helps businesses make better decisions.
vocabulary.translation: 数据分析帮助企业做出更明智的决策。

vocabulary.entry: chatbot /ˈtʃætbɒt/ n. 聊天机器人
vocabulary.example: The website uses a chatbot to answer customer queries.
vocabulary.translation: 这个网站使用聊天机器人回复客户咨询。

vocabulary.entry: wearable /ˈweərəbl/ n. 可穿戴设备（如智能手表、运动手环等）
vocabulary.example: She uses a wearable to track her daily steps.
vocabulary.translation: 她用可穿戴设备记录每天的步数。

vocabulary.entry: resonate with /ˈrezəneɪt wɪð/ 引起……的共鸣
vocabulary.example: His speech resonated with the audience.
vocabulary.translation: 他的演讲引起了观众的共鸣。

vocabulary.entry: tailor /ˈteɪlə(r)/ v. 定制；量身打造
vocabulary.example: We can tailor the service to your specific needs.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以根据你的具体需求定制服务。

vocabulary.entry: retain /rɪˈteɪn/ v. 留住；保留
vocabulary.example: The company needs to retain its best employees.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司需要留住最优秀的员工。

vocabulary.entry: wellbeing /ˌwelˈbiːɪŋ/ n. 健康；安康
vocabulary.example: The company cares about its employees' physical and mental wellbeing.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司关心员工的身心健康。

vocabulary.entry: rely solely on /rɪˈlaɪ ˈsəʊlli ɒn/ 仅仅依靠；完全依赖
vocabulary.example: You shouldn't rely solely on technology to solve the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 你不应该仅仅依靠技术来解决这个问题。

sentences.english: Now millennials look to leave their jobs within the first two years, and when they are seeking a position, they want to know the benefits they’ll get on top of their pay.
sentences.chinese: 现在，千禧一代往往在入职头两年就想离职，而且他们找工作时，除了薪水，还想知道能获得哪些福利。

sentences.english: These include half-price cinema tickets, cycle to work schemes and gym passes.
sentences.chinese: 这些福利包括半价电影票、骑行上班计划和健身卡。

sentences.english: But these perks come at a cost to an employer, and now technology is being used to discover if and when they offer value for money.
sentences.chinese: 但这些福利对雇主来说是有成本的，如今，企业正利用技术来判断这些福利是否和何时物有所值。

sentences.chinese: 其目的是避免在无人使用的福利上浪费资金，同时让公司能够定制福利内容，以吸引和留住合适的员工。

sentences.chinese: 一项研究发现，通过对参与者的表现进行量化，他们每月的活动量相当于增加了4.8天。

sentences.chinese: 看来，如果使用得当，技术可以加强员工与公司之间的联系，进而打造一支更快乐、更健康、更忠诚的员工队伍。

sentences.chinese: 但人力资源专家警告称，不应仅仅依靠技术来决定员工福利的提供。

sentences.chinese: 他们表示，需要更深入地了解新技术及其使用方式。
